profile: Design/source review of compiled draft 0890592eaf79ccb462f9635dd33e7536862685bb. Current product is ordinary principal-only document-root XSLT preview on Bosak 1.26.2 / 6a3372fc3b91e733b71a426cf40f26feaaeb3bcb. No typed/persistent integration or owner acceptance claimed.

answers.answer: Current BosakPreviewExecutor validates and uses CaptureTransform(new XDocumentNode(input), XsltCaptureOptions), retaining principal/secondary serialized bytes, messages, failures and denied resource receipts. Proposed SchemaXsltExecutable.Transform(operation, invocation, context) represents document-root matching and distinct global input; admit both roles in the same operation, once per unique snapshot. Source-free initialTemplate uses an empty admission array unless dynamic context adds node inputs. CompileXPath/Evaluate and SchemaXQueryCompiler.Compile/Evaluate map future diagnostic query previews; neither is a current Braid product command. No demonstrated current requirement for arbitrary initial sequences, streaming or selectable initial modes; unsupported profiles must refuse explicitly. Required gap: show the supported bounded capture route from the proposed operation-based Transform to existing XSLT capture semantics. XdmValue alone does not demonstrate capture of all outputs/messages/resource receipts or serialization limits. Core must map a supported existing route or supply a public operation-bound capture capability; Braid does not prescribe its API design.

Typed/persistent route explicitly remains open. Worker-local authorized reopen is a candidate, subject to actual Schema/XmlDb authorization and version retention; no broker or in-process fallback is selected or implicitly approved. Current worker-v1 transports retained bytes, not live provider handles. A new profile/protocol must bind authorized immutable store/snapshot version, provider/schema environment, source/fixture/configuration identities and exact engine identity, reject unavailable or changed versions, and recheck currentness before publication. Never serialize authority objects, leases or credentials as descriptive JSON identities. Protocol/profile changes invalidate old evidence. No demonstrated new Core transport signature is requested: transport and acquisition policy belong to Braid/provider owners.

Require acquisition rollback; foreign/missing snapshot refusal before getters; distinct match/global memberships; duplicate admission single-lease accounting; deferred result enumeration and serialization inside Run/RunAsync; cancellation before admission, during raw work and during drain; close/revocation with outstanding work; concurrent-close and reentry refusal within the explicitly qualified profile; and original failure plus reverse-order cleanup failures. A canceled wait must not release resources while raw work runs. Current parent cancellation/deadline kills and awaits the worker process tree; unsent results are discarded. Typed/persistent implementation must additionally prove reader/generation retention through raw completion or confirmed process termination and actual provider recovery. Session close/drain contracts appear to represent these needs; no additional lifetime signature is demonstrated by source review. Detached immutable output bytes may cross IPC; borrowed result graphs may not escape as live authority. Keep all late results subject to source/fixture/configuration/entitlement freshness checks.

Proposed future fixtures, not measured results: ordinary current preview baseline; original assessed decimal/list/union/nil/no-typed-value with preserve/strip and copied/foreign evidence controls; persistent two-version reader held while generation changes; distinct match/global documents and source-free named template; lazy nested result consumed during cancellation/close; timeout/kill followed by authorized reopen. Initial experiment limits: two admitted snapshots, 1024 cached values/snapshot, 10000 atoms/value, 1024 numeric digits and scale 128, with boundary/refusal controls. Retain current 8 MiB input/style bounds, 64 MiB frame bound, 30-second post-launch deadline and configured output/step/message limits; these do not bound memory or compilation. These are proposed experiment ceilings, not Core defaults or performance acceptance. Measure cold/warm compile/admission/execute/consume/cleanup, peak memory and cancellation latency on identified hardware; PF-01-09 performance budgets and actual typed/persistent candidate pins remain open. Product pin is 1.26.2/6a3372fc and Braid source is 0f1d949e; no proposal assembly reference, store upgrade, D01 extension, R4/C45 or native acceptance is claimed.
